Starting today, Runna subscribers can use the new "Adapt for Heat" feature, which automatically adjusts pace targets based on local temperature and humidity. Here are the details.

Runna adds heat-aware training tool

Personalised running coach app Runna today (the 17th) announced three updates aimed at supporting users throughout the entire training cycle, from training in hot weather to post-race recovery.

The new "Adapt for Heat" feature, available starting today, will help users identify cooler running windows and recommend adjusted pace targets based on feels-like temperature, training duration, and specific sessions.

The "Adapt for Heat" feature displays a colour-coded hourly weather forecast, allowing users to quickly grasp the best time slots for running sessions and plan accordingly.

Here is Runna's introduction to this new feature:

Runna also announced the relaunch of the "Post-Race Recovery Plan" feature. Once a user opens a race plan ranging from 5km to 50km, the system will automatically generate a corresponding programme. Runna head coach and former Olympian Steph Kessell said these plans are designed by professional coaches to help runners "reduce the risk of overtraining or injury".

Finally, the platform also announced a new feature called "Upcoming Plans" to be launched in August. This feature allows users to schedule multiple training plans in advance and seamlessly transition from one to the next upon completion, further streamlining long-term training.

Here is Runna's introduction to the benefits of the "Upcoming Plans" feature:

Plan a full year of training in minutes: runners can overlay races, phased goals, and training blocks, giving a clear overview of the entire year of training.
